svg.title: How SevenSleep decides what the bed does
svg.desc: Requests come from the app, shortcuts, buttons, the schedule and the bed's sensors. Each is given a side, passed through the layers that can stop it, and sent to the firmware. Sleep is followed by the sensors and steered by the autopilot.
svg.text: 3. May it change the bed? Strongest first
Acts for the side picked on it
A request names a side or both
Jobs for each side on its own
Yes: the change goes to both sides
No: only the side asked for
Is either side in away mode?
each keeps its timer and target
Linked: the app copies power, temperature and saved schedules; the server copies shortcuts, buttons, in-bed actions and the autopilot.
Scheduled jobs stay each side's own, and linking never merges two schedules. The flip is applied only where the server meets the firmware.
Is this side in away mode?
Looked at when a job is built or runs
Stops the schedule, warm-up and alarm,
Is tonight switched off in the schedule?
Each night has its own switch
No bed on or off, temperature change,
Turned on by hand, with the schedule paused?
Settings > Other. Lost in a restart
Stops bed on and off, temperature changes,
warm-up and the autopilot. Not alarms
From the warm-up time to the alarm
and the autopilot until the alarm
Someone asleep, with the autopilot on
Bed on or off, a temperature, the warm-up, the alarm
One setting every 10 minutes, never past 4°F from the base
These go through whatever the layers say
A change by hand: app, buttons, a shortcut
A one-time alarm, bed on or off
The alarm after a long time in bed
A temperature set by hand in the night
The autopilot holds it exactly, on either side,
until the end of that third of the night,
then learns from it and carries on
Each side is judged on its own
Away, warm-up and a hold stop that side only.
The autopilot moves only sides that are on,
Temperature is a level from -100 to 100 (50 to 108°F), so not every degree is a setting.
A side is on while its timer runs and turns off by itself at zero. An alarm is 3 minutes a request,
so the server chains them. One command at a time; the bed's answers are logged, not checked.
Goes by the side slept on
A side with a thing on it and no body is an empty side. Sleep is followed whether or not the autopilot is on; the bed is only moved when it is.
Each side's stay is saved on its own. With the sides linked, Data > Sleep shows the bed as one sleeper's: of stays that share hours, the one with the most sleep.
When the night ends, each side still set to what the autopilot put there is given what the schedule wants at that hour.
A record of the night (a tracker's by Shortcut, or times set by hand) is filed with the stay; from 7 nights the sleep rules are fitted to them.
1. Linked sides can keep two different schedules: each side's jobs still run, and the autopilot walks them together.
2. A night longer than 11.5 hours asks the bed for more than 12 hours on, which its firmware may cut short.
3. Flipping the sides takes the in-bed baselines and the empty-bed piezo level with it; press 'Bed is empty now' afterwards.
4. Priming does not check whether the bed is in use, and jobs missed during an update or reboot are not caught up.
